newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - July 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Figures released yesterday reveal that 16,900 full-time jobs were lost in June, bringing full-time employment to its lowest level since October 1995. The slump has renewed market calls for the Reserve Bank of Australia to again cut interest rates in an attempt to boost economic recovery. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard will next week initiate development of a policy blueprint for the information industry. Howard is expected to ask ministers to report to Cabinet with an integrated plan on the employment potential of the sector. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has personally addressed reputed comments by Normandy Mining head Robert Champion de Crespigny criticising his recent comments on the gold industry. Costello is believed to have telephoned de Crespigny claiming he had been misquoted over his attitude to the Reserve Bank's recent selling of its gold reserve. Page 1.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission is investigating whether NSW electricity retailers have breached trade practices law by offering backdated discounts to big power consumers. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The unemployment rate for June fell from 8.8 to 8.5 per cent with 11,900 new jobs being created. This slightly offset the 40,300 jobs lost in May but the good news was overshadowed by a 20,000 drop in the participation rate. Page 1.

Reserve Bank governor Ian Macfarlane yesterday defended the bank's decision to sell two-thirds of its gold reserves claiming the decision will save taxpayers $150 million a year. McLachlan further accused the gold industry of being largely responsible forthe recent plunge in global gold markets by exaggerating the impact of the bank's decision. Page 1.

The family of seven-year-old Renee Clark, who died as a result of an ambulance dispatch bungle, are demanding answers. They have called for an investigation into Intergraph the operators of the emergency dispatch service for the Metropolitan Ambulance Sevice. Page 1.

The Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union (CFMEU) has written to the Asian customers of mining giant Rio Tinto advising them they should consider more reliable Australian suppliers. Referring to the month-long strike at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valle coal mine, CFMEU warns that contracts worth over $200 million are now at risk. Page 2.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Uniting Church, the third-largest denomination in Australia, has postponed voting on a proposal allowing the ordination of homosexual clergy. At this week's Uniting Church assembly in Perth, Aboriginal and ethnic congregations succeeded in persuadingthe 261 delegates to defer any decision on the issue for three years. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard yesterday supported tax incentives encouraging married women to leave the workforce after figures showed that full-time employment had fallen to a record low. Speaking on Sydney radio, Howard said a proposal to increase the famly tax incentive to encourage approximately 200,000 parents who were not enthusiastic about working outside the home to relinquish their employment, had "enormous merits". Page 1.

The Federal Government has ordered four RAAF C-130 aircraft to begin evacuating Australian citizens from the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh. Australia has also threatened to cut aid to Cambodia following an escalation of violence in wake of the weekend cou. Page 1.

Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union president John Maitland has sent letters to Asian and local customers of Rio Tinto, warning them that the company's lucrative export contracts are at risk on account of the strike at Rio Tinto's Hunter Valley colliery which could extend over three months. The letters are considered to signal an escalation in the conflict, with the Hunter Valley mine manager Allan Davies condemning the move as irresponsible. Page 1.
THE AGE

Australia is to begin its first military-led evacuation operation today with three Hercules aircraft to rescue approximately 400 Australian, New Zealand, Canadian and Swedish citizens from strife-torn Cambodia. Federal Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander owner said yesterday he did not expect the operation to be dangerous and that it had been launched at the request of Australians in Cambodia. Page 1.

The Vic and SA Governments yesterday moved to relax national gun laws by easing restriction on ownership of multiple firearms. The proposal to abolish the "cooling off" period between obtaining a permit and buying a weapon for people with one firearm, wil be discussed at next week's meeting of State police ministers in Adelaide. Page 1.

Figures released yesterday show that Vic's unemployment rate has risen to 9.4 per cent in June, reflecting a continuing weak labour market nation-wide. The national unemployment rate fell from 8.8 to 8.5 per cent but this was largely the result of a fallin the participation rate of approximately 20,000. Page 1.

Australian Football League club Geelong has offered player Gary Ablett an ambassadorial role in an attempt to give the long-term team member a dignified retirement. Ablett has recently been experiencing lifestyle problems which have weakened his football performance and led to his being dropped by marketing company Club 10. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
